unit.title: Numbers and Operations Around Us
unit.about_unit: Explores how human travel, trade, measurement, and recording large quantities led to five-digit numbers (ten thousands), multi-digit multiplication, division arrays, and multiplicative reasoning.

facilitation_guide.headline: Real-World Contexts
facilitation_guide.text: Connect numbers with train tickets, odometer readings, and village populations.

facilitation_guide.headline: Base-10 Manipulatives
facilitation_guide.text: Emphasize grouping 10 of any unit into 1 of the next higher unit using visual tokens.

chapter.title: The Dairy Farm
chapter.tagline: Unlocking multiplication arrays, factors, multiples, and algebraic shape puzzles
chapter.overview: At the village dairy farm, Gopal packs pouches of milk and buttermilk in crate arrays. Children discover how rectangular packing layouts connect to factors and multiples, build factor trees, and solve shape algebra puzzles where geometric symbols hide secret numbers.

sections.title: The Dairy Mystery: Shape Equations
sections.subtitle: Deducing numbers between 1 and 24 hidden behind geometric shapes

storyNarrative.dialogue: Welcome to our dairy! Each shape represents a secret number. If Triangle + Triangle = Circle, and Circle × Triangle = 16, what number is hiding in the Triangle?

concept.heading: Early Algebraic Reasoning
concept.keyRule: Using substitution and number sense to find unknown values satisfying simultaneous relations.

sections.subtitle: Finding all rectangular arrangements for a given quantity

storyNarrative.dialogue: We have 24 buttermilk pouches to pack. We can arrange them as 1 × 24, 2 × 12, 3 × 8, or 4 × 6!

concept.heading: Factor Pairs as Rectangular Dimensions
concept.keyRule: The factors of a number N are the exact row and column dimensions of all rectangles that can be formed using N unit squares.

sections.subtitle: Breaking composite numbers down into prime building blocks

storyNarrative.dialogue: Like branches on a tree, we can split 36 into 6 × 6, and each 6 into 2 × 3! No matter which branches you pick first, the leaf numbers are always the same!

concept.keyRule: Every composite number can be broken down into a unique set of prime factor building blocks.
